tag.text: RCT · JAMA 2024 · 36 weeks on the drug, then drug or placebo

components.text: US real world: about 2 in 3 stop within a year

footnote: Source: SURMOUNT-4 (JAMA 2024), STEP 4 (JAMA 2021), STEP 1 extension (Diabetes Obes Metab 2022), BMJ 2026, China obesity guideline (2024)
notes: Every study agrees that weight comes back after stopping. In STEP 4, patients took semaglutide for 20 weeks and lost 10.6%, then were randomized for 48 weeks: those who continued lost another 7.9%, those switched to placebo regained 6.9%. In SURMOUNT-4, patients took tirzepatide for 36 weeks and lost 20.9%. Over the next 52 weeks, those who continued lost another 5.5% and those switched to placebo regained 14.0%. 89.5% of those who continued kept at least 80% of the weight they had lost, against 16.6% of those who stopped. A 2026 BMJ meta-analysis of 37 studies and 9,341 people found an average regain of 0.4 kg a month after stopping, with cardiometabolic measures back at baseline in about 1.4 years. US real-world data cited in China's obesity guideline show about two in three patients stop within a year. For the hospital this means two things. Patients must hear before they start that this is long-term treatment and that the cost is long-term too. And the stopping rules and follow-up belong in the control plan, not just the prescribing.
